title: Angle Sum of Triangles, Quadrilaterals and Polygons
seo_title: Year 7 Angle Sum Worksheets: Triangles, Quadrilaterals and Polygons (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: demonstrate that the interior angle sum of a triangle in the plane is 180° and apply this to determine the interior angle sum of other shapes and the size of unknown angles
meta_desc: Free Year 7 maths worksheets on angle sums for the Australian Curriculum (AC9M7M05): angles in triangles, isosceles and right-angled triangles, exterior angles, quadrilaterals and polygons. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: The angles in a triangle add up to 180°.
key_sub: A polygon with n sides splits into n − 2 triangles, so its angles add up to (n − 2) × 180°.
body_html:
How it works

The angles in a triangle add up to 180°: tear off the corners and they make a straight line.

  • An isosceles triangle has two equal sides and two equal base angles.
  • An equilateral triangle has three 60° angles.
  • An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles.
  • A quadrilateral splits into 2 triangles, so its angles add up to 360°.
  • A polygon with n sides splits into n − 2 triangles: angle sum = (n − 2) × 180°.
Example

Two angles of a triangle are 48° and 75°. Find the third.

180 − 48 − 75.

Answer: 57°

Example

An isosceles triangle has a top angle of 40°. Find each base angle.

180 − 40 = 140.

140 ÷ 2 = 70.

Answer: 70°

Example

Find the angle sum of a pentagon.

5 − 2 = 3 triangles.

3 × 180.

Answer: 540°

Common mistakes

  • Using 360° for a triangle, or 180° for a quadrilateral.
  • In an isosceles triangle, using the wrong pair of equal angles: the equal angles are opposite the equal sides.
  • Using n × 180° for a polygon instead of (n − 2) × 180°.
  • Forgetting that an exterior angle and its interior angle add to 180°.

faq.q: Why do the angles in a triangle add up to 180°?
faq.a: Tear off the three corners and put them together: they make a straight line, which is 180°.

faq.q: What do the angles in a quadrilateral add up to?
faq.a: 360°, because a quadrilateral splits into two triangles.

faq.q: How do I find the angle sum of any polygon?
faq.a: Use (n − 2) × 180°, where n is the number of sides. A hexagon: 4 × 180° = 720°.

faq.q: What is the exterior angle of a triangle?
faq.a: The angle between one side and the extension of the next side. It equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles.

items.q: A triangle has interior angles of 44° and 72°. The side next to the third angle is extended. What is the exterior angle there?
items.e: The exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles: 44 + 72 = 116°. (Or 180 − third angle 64°.)

items.q: A triangle has interior angles of 38° and 70°. The side next to the third angle is extended. What is the exterior angle there?
items.e: The exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles: 38 + 70 = 108°. (Or 180 − third angle 72°.)

items.q: A parallelogram has one angle of 65°. What are the other three angles?
items.e: Opposite angles are equal and neighbouring angles add to 180°: 65°, 115° and 115°.

items.q: Can a triangle have angles of 100° and 85°?
c: No, because 100° + 85° is already more than 180°
items.e: The three angles must add up to exactly 180°. So no.

items.q: Liam says the angles in a quadrilateral add up to 180°. Is he right?
items.e: A quadrilateral can be split into two triangles: 2 × 180° = 360°.

items.q: How many triangles can a hexagon be split into, using diagonals from one corner?
items.e: A polygon with n sides splits into n − 2 triangles: 6 − 2 = 4.

items.q: Why do the interior angles of a pentagon add up to 540°?
c: It splits into 3 triangles from one corner
items.e: From one corner you can draw 2 diagonals, making 3 triangles: 3 × 180° = 540°.

items.q: What is each interior angle of a regular hexagon?
Matilda says the interior angles of a hexagon add up to 6 × 180 = 1080°. What is the correct sum?
An isosceles triangle has one angle of 100°. What are the other two angles?
items.e: 100° must be the top angle (two 100° angles would be too big). (180 − 100) ÷ 2 = 40° each.

items.q: An isosceles triangle has one angle of 70°. Which could be the other two angles?
items.e: If 70° is the top angle, the base angles are 55° each. If 70° is a base angle, the angles are 70°, 70° and 40°. Both are possible.

items.q: The angles of a quadrilateral are all equal. What is each angle?
What is the sum of the interior angles of an octagon?
A triangle has an exterior angle of 120° at one corner. What is the interior angle at that corner?
items.e: They lie on a straight line: 180 − 120 = 60°.
